Open a dataset from a file or URL

Source: R/open.R
open_dataset.Rd

Read a multidimensional data source into an ndr Dataset, through one of two engines:

Usage

open_dataset(dsn, vars = NULL, ..., group = NULL, engine = NULL)

Arguments

dsn

Data source name. A file path, URL, or GDAL connection string (e.g. 'ZARR:"/vsicurl/https://example.com/store.parq"').

vars

Character vector of variable names to include. Default NULL includes all data variables. Use character() for schema + coords only. All variables are loaded lazily on first access via $.

...

Passed to zaro::zaro() for the "zaro" engine (e.g. anonymous = TRUE, region =); otherwise unused.

group

Path of the group to open in a nested store, e.g. "measurements/reflectance/r10m". Default NULL, the root group (or the group named in dsn after .zarr/, see Details).

engine

"gdal" or "zaro". The default picks "zaro" for zaro objects and for s3://, gs://, virtualizarr://, byterefs://, mdimrefs://, flatrefs:// and reference+json:///reference+parquet:// sources, and for local or http(s):// paths ending in .zarr (or with a group after it) when zaro is installed; else "gdal" (including ZARR: connection strings and /vsi paths).

Value

A Dataset with coordinates, global attributes, and lazy data variables whose values are read only when used.

Details

  • "gdal": any source GDAL's multidim API can read (NetCDF, HDF5, Zarr v2/v3, kerchunk-parquet virtual stores, VRT multidim), from local paths, /vsicurl/, /vsis3/ and other GDAL virtual filesystems. Needs the GDAL7 package (remotes::install_github("rgdal-dev/GDAL7"), GDAL >= 3.10).

  • "zaro": Zarr V2/V3 and virtual Zarr (kerchunk, VirtualiZarr Parquet, mdim-refs) read by the zaro package (remotes::install_github("hypertidy/zaro")), with no GDAL in the path. Takes anything zaro::zaro() opens, such as s3:// and gs:// URIs, virtualizarr://, byterefs:// (or mdimrefs://) and flatrefs:// (a byterefs flat refs store, read by row group) sources, or a store or zaro::zaro_dataset() object.

Reading data needs the altarr package (remotes::install_github("hypertidy/altarr")).

Lazy loading

open_dataset() reads only coordinates and metadata. Accessing a data variable via ds$var_name returns a DataArray whose data is a lazy chunked array (see lazy-data): still no array data is read. sel() and isel() stay lazy, reductions stream the array chunk by chunk, and arithmetic or collect() read the selected values. This allows opening large datasets (e.g. 12TB BRAN2023) without reading any array data. Use vars to limit which variables are available. Lazy reads need the altarr package (remotes::install_github("hypertidy/altarr")).

Variable classification

Arrays are classified as coordinates or data variables based on CF conventions: a 1D array whose name matches its dimension name is treated as a coordinate. Every other array with one or more dimensions is a data variable, including 1D arrays along another dimension (such as a mean per band) and bounds arrays (e.g. time_bnds). Scalar arrays are skipped.

Numeric and logical data variables are lazy. String data variables can't be (lazy arrays are numeric), so they are read at open when they have at most getOption("ndr.eager_string_max", 1e6) elements, and skipped with a message when larger. String coordinates are read like any other. The GDAL engine reads strings with GDAL7 from rgdal-dev/GDAL7#15; with an older GDAL7 it skips string arrays with a message (string coordinates too, leaving that dimension without coordinate values).

Coordinate types

Regular spatial grids (equal spacing within floating-point tolerance) are stored as ImplicitCoord (offset + step, no data allocation). Irregular grids and time coordinates are stored as ExplicitCoord.

CF time decoding

Time dimensions (GDAL type "TEMPORAL") are automatically decoded from their CF units (e.g. "days since 1800-01-01") to R Date or POSIXct values using cf_decode_time().

The zaro engine

Consolidated metadata is one request for the whole store. Data variables are CF-decoded as they are read: fill and missing values read as NA, and scale_factor/add_offset are applied. Those attributes move from the Variable's attrs to its encoding. Arrays without dimension names get names from zaro (see zaro::zaro_dataset()).

Arrays a store can't decode

A byterefs store (byterefs://) names the arrays whose codecs zaro does not know, rather than let them be misread (byterefs decision 0007). zaro warns about them at open; the Dataset leaves them out of its coordinates and variables, lists them with the reason when printed, and asking for one (ds$v, vars = "v") is an error giving the reason.

Georeferenced grids

A georeferenced grid becomes one AffineIndex, by the same rules in both engines:

  • GeoZarr (spatial:dimensions, spatial:transform, spatial:registration, optional spatial:shape, on the group or the data variable): the transform defines the grid, so the x/y coordinate arrays are not read. The CRS comes from proj:code, proj:wkt2 or proj:projjson, else the CF grid mapping.

  • CF: a data variable whose grid_mapping variable has crs_wkt (or spatial_ref), and whose first two dims (R order) have regular coordinates.

  • GDAL engine only, before the CF route: a data variable with a CRS from GDAL whose HORIZONTAL_X / HORIZONTAL_Y dimensions (as netCDF declares them) have regular coordinates.

Groups

A nested store (e.g. an EOPF Sentinel-2 product or other GeoZarr) keeps its arrays in groups below the root. Open one group with group =, or name it in the path: "https://host/product.zarr/measurements/r10m" is read as dsn = "https://host/product.zarr", group = "measurements/r10m", so the store's consolidated metadata (at its root) is used. The group's attributes become the Dataset's. List a store's groups with zaro::zaro_groups().

Dimension ordering

Arrays are stored in R's column-major (Fortran) order, matching GDAL7's read_mdarray() $gis$dim convention. Dimension names follow the same order. For a NetCDF variable with dimensions (time, lat, lon), the R array has dim = c(nlon, nlat, ntime) and dims = c("lon", "lat", "time").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Open lazily - no data read yet
ds <- open_dataset("sst.mnmean.nc")
ds  # shows variables with [not loaded]

# Selecting is lazy too; collect() reads just the selected values
ds$sst |> sel(time = as.Date("2020-06-15"), lat = c(-60, -30)) |> collect()

# Reductions stream the array chunk by chunk
ds$sst |> sel(lat = c(-60, -30)) |> nd_mean("time", na.rm = TRUE)

# Scope to specific variables (still lazy)
ds <- open_dataset("sst.mnmean.nc", vars = "sst")

# Remote kerchunk-parquet - only sst schema, 12TB never touched
dsn <- 'ZARR:"/vsicurl/https://example.com/store.parq"'
ds <- open_dataset(dsn, vars = "temp")
ds$temp  # a lazy DataArray: nothing read yet

# One group of a nested (sharded GeoZarr) store
eopf <- paste0("https://s3.explorer.eopf.copernicus.eu/esa-zarr-sentinel-explorer-fra/",
               "tests-output/sentinel-2-l2a/",
               "S2C_MSIL2A_20260120T084301_N0511_R064_T36UXA_20260120T122910.zarr")
r10m <- open_dataset(eopf, group = "measurements/reflectance/r10m")
r10m$b04 |> isel(x = 5001:6000, y = 5001:6000) |> collect()
} # }
